details:
Project Title: LUNA-LINK – Intelligent Lunar Landing Site Navigator


LUNA-LINK is a proposed intelligent lunar landing site navigation system designed to help researchers and future space missions identify and compare suitable landing locations on the Moon, particularly near the lunar south pole.

Selecting a safe lunar landing location is challenging because of uneven terrain, deep shadows, changing sunlight conditions and limitations in communication with Earth. Our project aims to make this process easier by providing a visual platform to explore different lunar locations and understand their environmental conditions.

The proposed system allows users to explore lunar landing locations and compare different sites and mission dates. It focuses on visualizing the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon, helping users understand sunlight opportunities and potential Earth communication visibility windows.

The project uses NASA lunar datasets and scientific information, including Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Wide Angle Camera (WAC) data, as proposed data sources for understanding lunar surface features and terrain conditions. Sun and Earth geometry will also be considered to study illumination and visibility.

The major benefits of LUNA-LINK include supporting better landing-site comparisons, improving awareness of lunar environmental conditions and helping users understand the challenges involved in planning future lunar missions.

What makes our project creative is its combination of lunar terrain exploration, Sun and Earth visibility concepts, and interactive site comparison in one easy-to-understand navigation platform. Instead of considering only the physical landing location, it also considers how environmental conditions change with location and time.

Our team considered scientific relevance, accessibility of NASA datasets, visualization, usability and the practical challenges of future lunar exploration while developing this concept.

Our ultimate goal is to contribute to safer, smarter and more informed lunar exploration through accessible data visualization and innovative navigation ideas.
